nrc-skin-renderer
========

Three.js powered Minecraft skin, cosmetic and emote renderer.

# Features
* Skins (classic and slim)
* NRC cosmetics in the Bedrock/GeckoLib format (`.geo.json`, `.animation.json`, `.norisk.json`)
* Emotes, including props and particle effects
* Capes
* Minecraft style name tag with rank or creator code icon
* Animated textures (`.png.mcmeta`)
* Particle systems (`.particle.json`)
* Linear, catmullrom and step keyframe interpolation
* Molang expressions in keyframes
* Shimmer loading skeleton with crossfade
* Promo outline post effect

# Usage

```bash
yarn add nrc-skin-renderer three react @react-three/fiber
```

`three` is a required peer dependency. `react` and `@react-three/fiber` are only needed for the `/react` entry, `/core` is plain three.js.

```tsx
import { SkinRenderer } from "nrc-skin-renderer/react";

<SkinRenderer
  textureUrl="img/skin.png"
  variant="slim"
  cosmetics={[
    {
      id: "8b2e9f5a",
      type: "HAT",
      urls: {
        geo: "cosmetics/crown/crown.geo.json",
        texture: "cosmetics/crown/crown.png",
        animation: "cosmetics/crown/crown.animation.json",
        metadata: "cosmetics/crown/crown.norisk.json",
      },
    },
  ]}
  emote={{ animation: "emotes/idle.animation.json" }}
  nametag={{ text: "Player", iconUrl: "img/rank.png" }}
  loading={false}
  style={{ width: 460, height: 620 }}
/>
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `textureUrl` | `string \| null` | required | Skin texture url or data url |
| `variant` | `"classic" \| "slim"` | `"classic"` | Player model |
| `cosmetics` | `SkinRendererCosmetic[]` | `[]` | Cosmetics mounted on the rig |
| `cape` | `string \| SkinRendererCape \| null` | `null` | Cape texture url, or `{ texture, mcmeta, elytra }` |
| `emote` | `EmoteAssetUrls \| null` | `null` | Looping emote animation, optionally with prop geo and texture |
| `nametag` | `SkinRendererNametag \| null` | `null` | Name tag above the head |
| `outline` | `boolean \| Partial<PromoOutlineConfig>` | `true` | Promo outline post effect |
| `spinSpeed` | `number` | `0` | Auto rotation in rad/s, `0` enables drag rotation |
| `rotation` | `number` | `0` | Turns the rig from its resting pose, in radians. `Math.PI` shows the back |
| `zoom` | `number` | `1` | Pulls the camera in, `2` fills twice as much of the frame |
| `draggable` | `boolean` | `true` | Mouse and touch drag rotation, sideways and up to 60 degrees up or down, about the rig's middle |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | Shows the shimmer skeleton, fades out when set back to `false` |
| `skeletonColor` | `string` | violet | Accent color of the loading skeleton |

## Cosmetics

A cosmetic is `{ id, type, urls }`. The `urls` object points at the cosmetic's asset files:

```ts
interface CosmeticAssetUrls {
  geo: string;
  texture: string;
  animation?: string;
  metadata?: string;
  metadataJson?: unknown;
  mcmeta?: string;
  particles?: ParticleAssetEntry[];
}
```

The renderer fetches nothing on its own. The consumer resolves asset urls (pack index, CDN, CMS) and passes them in, so the same component works in the launcher, the website or anywhere else.

## Emotes

```tsx
<SkinRenderer textureUrl="img/skin.png" emote={{ animation: "emotes/wave.animation.json" }} />
```

Emotes with props ship a `geo` and `texture` next to the animation:

```tsx
<SkinRenderer
  textureUrl="img/skin.png"
  emote={{
    animation: "emotes/gamingchair.animation.json",
    geo: "emotes/gamingchair.geo.json",
    texture: "emotes/gamingchair.png",
  }}
/>
```

## Name Tag

```tsx
<SkinRenderer textureUrl="img/skin.png" nametag={{ text: "Player" }} />

<SkinRenderer
  textureUrl="img/skin.png"
  nametag={{ text: "Player", iconUrl: "img/rank.png", iconPlus: true }}
/>
```

`iconPlus` selects the second frame of a two frame icon strip (NRC+ variant). The default font is `MinecraftTen` with a `Minecraft` fallback. Load it with a `@font-face` rule:

```css
@font-face {
  font-family: "MinecraftTen";
  src: url("/fonts/minecraft-ten.woff2") format("woff2");
}
```

## Loading Skeleton

While `loading` is `true` the renderer shows an animated shimmer silhouette of the player and name tag. When `loading` switches to `false` the skeleton crossfades into the real rig.

```tsx
<SkinRenderer textureUrl={skin} loading={isLoading} skeletonColor="#00b9e8" />
```

## Outline

The promo outline is enabled by default. Pass a config to tune it or `false` to disable it:

```tsx
<SkinRenderer textureUrl={skin} outline={{ strength: 2.8, thickness: 2, sensitivity: 0.4 }} />

<SkinRenderer textureUrl={skin} outline={false} />
```

## Snapshots

`nrc-skin-renderer/snapshot` renders stills off screen, for skin lists, previews and
anywhere a live canvas would be wasteful. It needs no React.

```ts
import { SkinSnapshotRenderer } from "nrc-skin-renderer/snapshot";

const renderer = new SkinSnapshotRenderer(360, 504);

const blob = await renderer.snapshot({
  textureUrl: "img/skin.png",
  variant: "slim",
  cosmetics: [{ id: "8b2e9f5a", type: "HAT", urls: { /* … */ } }],
  emote: { animation: "emotes/idle.animation.json" },
  emoteTime: 1.4,
  bones: { bipedRightArm: { rotation: [-110, 0, 0] } },
});

renderer.dispose();
```

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `textureUrl` | `string` | required | Skin texture url or data url |
| `variant` | `"classic" \| "slim"` | `"classic"` | Player model |
| `cosmetics` | `SnapshotCosmetic[]` | `[]` | Same shape the React renderer takes |
| `cape` | `string \| SnapshotCape \| null` | `null` | Cape texture url, or `{ texture, mcmeta }` for an animated one |
| `view` | `"front" \| "back" \| "left" \| "right"` | `"front"` | Turns the rig a quarter at a time, keeping the slight angle of the resting pose |
| `body` | `boolean` | `true` | `false` hides the player, leaving only what is worn |
| `fit` | `boolean \| number` | `false` | Frames whatever is visible instead of the whole rig. A number sets the margin |
| `crop` | `boolean \| number` | `false` | Trims the transparent border off the result. A number sets the padding as a fraction of the content |
| `fov` | `number` | `40` | Vertical field of view in degrees |
| `focus` | `number` | `0.5` | Where in the framed box the camera aims, `0` at the feet and `1` at the head. Needs `fit` |
| `emote` | `EmoteAssetUrls \| null` | `null` | Poses the rig with an emote |
| `emoteTime` | `number` | `0` | Seconds into the emote to freeze at |
| `bones` | `Record<string, BonePose> \| null` | `IDLE_POSE` | Manual pose, applied after the emote. `null` keeps the rest pose |
| `rotation` | `number` | `0` | Extra turn on top of the resting pose, in radians |
| `outline` | `boolean \| Partial<PromoOutlineConfig>` | `true` | Promo outline post effect |

`snapshot()` resolves to a `Blob`, `image/webp` at quality `0.9` unless
`{ mimeType, quality }` say otherwise.

Set `elytra` on a cape to render it as elytra wings instead. The wing shape comes
from the texture's transparency, not from geometry - the model is two boxes, and
the game only draws the pixels that pass its alpha test. A fully painted texture
therefore renders as a slab, in this renderer and in the game alike.

The wings use the
vanilla model and read the vanilla cape layout, texture offset 22,0 in a 64x32
sheet, the same mapping the game and skinview3d use. A cape drawn in another
layout has no art there and will come out wrong, which is true of every renderer
that follows the vanilla mapping.

A cape on the player is `{ cape, view: "back" }`. For a cape list, drop the player
and let the cape fill the frame:

```ts
await renderer.snapshot({
  textureUrl: steveSkin,
  cape: { texture: capeUrl, mcmeta: capeMcmetaUrl },
  view: "back",
  body: false,
  fit: true,
});
```

`textureUrl` is still required there, since the rig is built either way; it just is
not drawn.
 Capes that ship a `.png.mcmeta` are frame
strips, so pass the `mcmeta` url along or the whole strip lands on the cape. A cape
that already exists as a cosmetic can go through `cosmetics` instead, which picks up
its metadata on its own.

Without an emote or an explicit `bones` object a still uses `IDLE_POSE`, the pose the
launcher renders its skins in, so a preview does not read as a mannequin. Pass
`bones: null` for the plain rest pose, or your own object to replace it. Note that an
empty object is a pose that sets nothing, not a request for the default.

Bone poses use the same convention as Bedrock animation files: degrees, with the X
and Y axes negated, so values can be lifted straight out of a `.animation.json`.
Bone names come from `BipedBones` and `ArmorBones`; positions are offsets from the
rest pose.

```ts
bones: {
  bipedHead: { rotation: [0, 25, 0] },
  bipedRightArm: { rotation: [-110, 0, 0], position: [0, 1, 0] },
}
```

`fit` frames the rig; `crop` then trims what is left over, so the image carries the
content's own aspect and a container can scale it without letterboxing. A skin's
second layer is geometry even where its texture is transparent, so both work off
the drawn pixels rather than the bounding box.

One WebGL context is shared and requests are queued, since browsers cap how many
live contexts a document may hold. Call `dispose()` when a batch is done; the next
`snapshot()` builds a fresh context.

The still and the live `SkinRenderer` read their pose, camera, lighting and renderer
settings from the same constants, so both look alike.

## Core

`nrc-skin-renderer/core` exposes the engine without React:

```ts
import {
  loadCosmetic,
  loadEmote,
  buildBoneTree,
  steveGeoForVariant,
  EmotePlayer,
  applyEmoteToRig,
  ParticleSystem,
} from "nrc-skin-renderer/core";
```

| Entry | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `nrc-skin-renderer/core` | Parsing and runtime for geo, animations, emotes and particles |
| `nrc-skin-renderer/react` | `SkinRenderer`, `CosmeticGeoViewer`, `SteveRig`, `EmoteViewer` and hooks |
| `nrc-skin-renderer/snapshot` | `SkinSnapshotRenderer`, off screen stills |
| `nrc-skin-renderer/postfx` | Promo outline pipeline for the EffectComposer |

# Playground

A dev-only gallery that renders **every** NRC cosmetic on a Steve body so you can
eyeball that they all look right.

```bash
yarn install
yarn dev
```

Open the printed `localhost` url. The grid lazily mounts one renderer per visible
tile (browsers cap live WebGL contexts), with category filter and search.

Cosmetics are read from the local **NoRiskClient launcher cache** (no network, no
auth), so you need the launcher installed. Defaults to the `norisk-prod` V3 cache:

```
%APPDATA%/norisk/NoRiskClientV3/meta/assets/noriskclient/indexes/norisk-prod.json
%APPDATA%/norisk/NoRiskClientV3/meta/assets/noriskclient/norisk-prod/objects/<hash[:2]>/<hash>
```

Point it elsewhere (another install, `norisk-dev`) with env vars:

```bash
NRC_INDEX=/path/to/indexes/norisk-prod.json \
NRC_OBJECTS=/path/to/norisk-prod/objects \
yarn dev
```

The playground lives in `playground/` and is not part of the published package.

# Build

```bash
yarn install
yarn build
```

Outputs ESM and type declarations to `dist/`.
